author: reek
body: Draws the cloud model to the GOP framebuffer: one ray per traced sample, composited over a sky gradient.

author: reek
body: What keeps it tractable at all is that most rays do almost nothing. A step below the density floor never runs the light march, and `c-density` returns before evaluating the detail sum whenever the base shape has already lost. The expensive path is only paid inside cloud.

author: reek
body: The traced grid. Each traced sample fills a 2x2 block.

author: reek
body: The buffer is cleared to a flat colour before drawing. The GOP surface comes up as whatever was in RAM, which is zeros, and zeros are black; a capture that fires before the last row is drawn then shows a black band that is indistinguishable from a rendered night sky. Clearing to a colour that appears nowhere else in the image makes an unfinished frame obvious instead of plausible. That is not hypothetical -- the first capture of this scene was a partial draw and read as a horizon.

author: reek
body: A right-handed basis built from a forward direction. The camera looks along +z and a little above the horizon, turned toward the sun so the forward-scattering rim the phase function produces is actually in frame. A cloud shader pointed away from its own sun looks like nothing at all.

author: reek
body: The background the clouds are composited over. Zenith to horizon by height, plus the sun's disc and its halo.

author: reek
body: One traced sample: trace the clouds, composite over the sky. The march already carries premultiplied scattered light, so the composite is the straight `scattered + background * transmittance` and needs no divide.
